title: Safety-gate evaluation workflow for model pins and version rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's model pin/upgrade flows (both catalog-managed and customer-pinned variants) currently change model versions without consistently running deterministic quality checks. This leads to intermittent regressions discovered only after customer incidents or manual QA. We need an automated safety gate that runs lightweight and full evals when a pin/upgrade is applied, surfaces diffs in the Console, and enforces configurable gating policies (warn, block, or auto-rollback) to reduce customer-facing regressions.

Scope and goals:
- Trigger automated evals whenever a model version is pinned or a catalog model is upgraded (catalog-owned rollouts and customer-initiated pins).
- Support a two-stage evaluation: quick smoke checks (latency, generation sanity, core metrics) followed by full eval (task-specific suites) when smoke passes.
- Persist results in the Console with diffs, representative examples, and a pass/fail decision.
- Expose gating policies per-catalog-entry and per-customer: warn-only, block rollout, or auto-rollback if thresholds are exceeded.
- Honor privacy/air-gapped constraints: private/on-prem customers can opt into local eval runners; if not available, surface a manual check requirement.

Out of scope:
- Building new eval metrics from scratch (we will reuse existing eval harness and eval suites).
- Automatic retraining or model selection beyond rollback/fallback.
context: Recent regression incidents (Q4 2025) where minor backend kernel changes and a model pin caused a 3-5% drop in factuality metrics for a high-value customer. PMs and SREs identified that there was no enforced eval gate at time of pin. There are existing tickets that touch the eval runner (ENG-4012) and model-catalog eventing (ENG-3721). This ticket consolidates product requirements and acceptance criteria for the safety gate feature.
proposed_solution:
1) Event hooks: extend model-catalog and pin APIs to emit a standardized 'pin_or_upgrade' event with metadata (model_id, old_version, new_version, initiating_user, catalog_flag).
2) Eval orchestration: on event, schedule a lightweight smoke eval (fast subset of evals) against a stored baseline (previous pinned version). If smoke passes thresholds, enqueue full eval job.
3) Baselines: default baseline = previous pinned version. For catalog upgrades, also compute a catalog baseline (curated canonical perf).
4) Gating: evaluate configured thresholds (absolute and relative) for key metrics; allow per-catalog-entry policy and per-customer overrides. Actions: WARN (record and notify), BLOCK (prevent pin/upgrade finalization until manual override), AUTO-ROLLBACK (if enabled for Dedicated/Private and threshold exceeded).
5) Console UX: new 'Pin Safety' panel on model detail showing pass/fail badge, metric diffs, top failure cases, and a one-click rollback/manual-approve action.
6) Notifications and audit: push evaluations to model audit logs, send optional Slack/email alerts to owners and to onboarding SREs if customer-tier is enterprise.
7) Cost and scheduling: heavy full-evals run in off-peak windows; sampling for very large customer suites to limit cost; daily budget cap per account configurable.
acceptance_criteria: When a user pins a new model version in the Console, a smoke eval is automatically scheduled and visible in the model's evaluation timeline.
If smoke eval fails according to the catalog policy, the Console shows a BLOCK state and the pin does not become active without manual override; an email/Slack alert is sent to the model owner.
If smoke eval passes, the full eval runs automatically and results are persisted with pass/fail and metric diffs versus baseline in Console UI within 24 hours.
Catalog upgrades trigger the same flow with an option to compare against the curated catalog baseline as well as the previous pinned version.
Admin UI allows configuring per-catalog-entry and per-customer gating policies and an enterprise customer can opt-in to AUTO-ROLLBACK for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Private/on-prem customers without networked eval runners receive a clear manual-check required state and an audit entry; no silent blocking of pinned versions unless customer has local eval runner enabled.
Evaluation runs are rate-limited and respect per-account daily budget caps; audit logs include cost estimate and actual cost for transparency.
End-to-end tests cover event generation (mock catalog), smoke vs full eval handoffs, gating decision logic, and Console rendering of results.
Docs updated: API docs for pin events, Console help content, and runbook for manual overrides and rollbacks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Spec + API): finalize event schema and gating policy model; define smoke eval subset and thresholds; create API contract for pin_or_upgrade event. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Infra): implement event emission in catalog/pinning service, wire to eval runner with a new lightweight job type; implement baseline selection logic. (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (Gating + Console): gating engine implementation, per-entry policy storage, Console 'Pin Safety' UI and notifications. (3 weeks)
Phase 4 (Pilot): enable for internal catalog entries and 3 enterprise pilot customers; observe metrics and tune thresholds. (2 weeks)
Phase 5 (Gradual roll): enable WARN for all catalog pins, then BLOCK for catalog-critical models, then opt-in AUTO-ROLLBACK for Dedicated customers only. (4 weeks)
Phase 6 (Full launch): enable configurable defaults; update docs and runbooks; hand off to support/success.
metrics: % of pins with an automated smoke eval scheduled
Number of blocked pins per week and manual overrides
Regression incidence rate after pin (customers reporting quality drops) — target reduction 60% in first 3 months
Daily cost of eval jobs and cost per evaluated pin
False positive/block rate (pins blocked but later manually approved without rollback)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Eval cost spikes if full suites run for every pin. Mitigation: default to smoke eval then conditional full eval; sampling and off-peak scheduling; budget caps.
Risk: Private/air-gapped customers can't run hosted evals. Mitigation: support local eval runners and surface manual-check states in Console; allow on-prem eval artifacts upload.
Risk: Blocking UX friction for fast-moving teams. Mitigation: make policy default WARN for non-critical models; expose easy manual-approve and audit trails.
Risk: Inconsistent baselines across catalog and customer contexts. Mitigation: record exact baseline version used and present multiple comparison views in Console.
notes: We should include a simple 'skip-eval' flag for emergency ops with audit logging; this must be limited to a small guardrail group and require two-person approval. Evaluate integrating with existing rollout automation so blocked pins can either be retried post-fix or automatically revert to previous stable model variant.
